metas.name: Camera Meta - Gen 4 coverage
metas.note: Generation 4 coverage in Alaska is concentrated around the city of Anchorage.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Camera Meta - Shitcam
metas.note: Shitcam is only found around Anchorage and Fairbanks, and parts of the road that connects them.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Taylor (East of Chicken)
metas.note: Taylor Highway (5), from the Yukon border to Tetlin Junction, can be recognized by the foggy, rainy weather, and Generation 2 camera. East of Chicken, the road is unpaved.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Taylor (West of Chicken)
metas.note: Taylor Highway (5), from the Yukon border to Tetlin Junction, can be recognized by the foggy, rainy weather, and Generation 2 camera. West of Chicken, the road is paved.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Alaskan Pipeline
metas.note: The Alaskan pipeline which is usually visible from main roads, can be seen at these points. This is an easy way to identify Alaska as there are no similar pipelines in the rest of the US.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Anchorage Hydrant
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically pale pink or pale yellow in colour.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Fairbanks Hydrant
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Fairbanks are commonly either bright yellow or a combination of colours (most commonly yellow and blue).
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Agricultural Fields
metas.note: Due to Alaska’s very cold climate; agricultural fields are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Alexander Archipelago (Gen 2)
metas.note:
The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Alexander Archipelago Landscape
metas.note:
The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood.

NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Denali Highway
metas.note: The Denali highway (8), stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly gravel highway in the ‘Alaska’ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Juneau
metas.note: Juneau, Alaska’s Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more ‘built up’ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Kenai Peninsula
metas.note: The Kenai peninsula can be recognized by its massive amount of fireweed along the roads. Most of the coverage is Gen 3 Autumn. Along AK-1 you will often see a bay to the west with mountains on the other side.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched

metas.name: Landscape - Max North Landscape
metas.note: The North end of the Dalton Highway (11) features a flat and snowy landscape and an overcast sky. A small ridge of hills can be seen to the west of the highway in certain spots.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Prudhoe Bay
metas.note: Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost town in America covered by street view, can be recognized by cold, dead landscape, overcast clouds and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car can sometimes be seen.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Steese Highway
metas.note: The Steese Highway (6) is a gravel highway that goes from Fairbanks to the town of ‘Central.’ Similar to the Denali highway, this road runs generally east to west and is covered in generation 2. The difference, however, is that the mountains along this road are noticeably lower than the ones adjacent to the Denali Highway.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Suburban Area with Mountains
metas.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Suburban Area without Mountains
metas.note: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Compared to Anchorage, the landscape is flatter.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Tundra
metas.note: Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Urban Coverage
metas.note: The only two major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Trekker - Black Beanie Trekker
metas.note: The trekker’s black and white bandana can only be seen in Nome.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Trekker - Shrekker
metas.note: Nome, Unalakleet and Galena are three isolated Alaskan towns which are covered only by trekker. The trekker’s lime green hat can be seen.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Aspen Trees
metas.note: Aspen trees (Populus tremuloides) can be found in lower elevation areas of interior and south-central regions of Alaska. These trees have white bark and rounded leaves.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt
